hani: FYI ran through the Python quickstart for new hires and hit a chain of small DX bugs that together block onboarding. Posting notes.
julie: ugh, sorry about that 44e what did you see?
hani: Path: `docs/quickstarts/python/getting-started/`
Problems: 1) README shows `import redwood` but package in setup.cfg is `redwood_inference` -> ModuleNotFoundError. 2) Example mixes sync/async: calls `resp = client.generate('hi')` in top-level code; the SDK method is async so you get a coroutine. 3) The sample's helper script has `#!/usr/bin/python` shebang which breaks in many distros. 4) README links to `https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md` which 404s.
sam: Can you paste the exact snippet?
hani: Yep, offending block:```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
resp = client.generate("Hello")
print(resp.text)
```
julie: Classic ordering problems. New users copy/paste and hit `TypeError` or `ModuleNotFoundError`.
hani: Also the README uses `pip install -e .` but the package metadata uses `name = redwood-inference` so editable install produces a different import path.
sam: Fix plan: either change packaging to expose `redwood` as top-level package, or update docs to `import redwood_inference as redwood` and show `from redwood_inference import Client`.
julie: For async we should show two variants: a minimal sync wrapper and the proper async pattern. Example corrections to include in README:```python
# async example
import asyncio
from redwood_inference import Client

async def main():
    client = Client(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
    resp = await client.generate("Hello")
    print(resp.text)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

# sync convenience wrapper
def generate_sync(prompt):
    import asyncio
    from redwood_inference import Client
    client = Client(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
    return asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(client.generate(prompt))
```
hani: Also recommend using `#!/usr/bin/env python3` in scripts and `ENTRYPOINT ["python3", "-u", "./start.py"]` in Dockerfile. Add a one-liner about Alpine vs Debian (alpine needs `python3` and `py3-pip`).
sam: Good catch about editable installs and package names. I'll open a tiny packaging PR that maps `redwood` -> `redwood_inference` as a compatibility shim (or we update docs whichever is less risky).
julie: Link checker alert: `link-checker` just posted a failure for the CONTRIBUTING.md link.
link-checker: [automated] link-checker: found broken link in `docs/quickstarts/python/getting-started/README.md` at 1865432140 -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md (404).
build-bot: Suggest adding CI smoke tests to samples job: `python -c "import redwood_inference"` and `python -c "import asyncio; asyncio.run(main())"` to catch import/async regressions.
hani: +1 on small CI checks. Also add a docs note about running examples in REPLs vs scripts (common confusion).
sam: I'll include these changes in a single PR: docs + sample Dockerfile + small CI test + packaging shim. Will tag `devex` and `docs`.
julie: main-only merge is fine. Please @mention me for a quick review.
hani: Thanks — will follow up with PR link and changelog blurb so support can point new users to the fix. :sparkles:
